title: Psychological Resources of Professional Development and Psychological Well-Being of College and University Students Under Uncertainty Stress
abstract: Latest social challenges have increased the interest in uncertainty stress research. These studies are particularly relevant in the context of young people's professional development and psychological well-being, given the increasing uncertainty of both the professional world and life in general. Therefore, it is important to study the psychological resources that contribute to the professional development and psychological well-being of students under uncertainty stress. This study aimed to analyze the psychological resources of professional development and psychological well-being under uncertainty stress in students of secondary vocational and higher educational institutions. Methods. Survey methods were used to diagnose psychological resources, uncertainty stress, professional development, and psychological well-being. Statistical analysis included correlation analysis and structural equation modeling (SEM). Sample: 1,822 students (935 college students and 887 university students). Results. Conscious self-regulation is a universal resource for professional development and psychological well-being under uncertainty stress. For the first time, the specificity of psychological resources under the various types of uncertainty stress was described. The results showed that under conditions of objective uncertainty stress, psychological well-being makes the most significant positive contribution to professional development, whereas under conditions of subjective uncertainty stress, the contributions of well-being and the level of conscious self-regulation are almost equal. Hardiness is a significant resource, mitigating the impact of subjective and objective uncertainty stress on psychological well-being, whereas dispositional optimism becomes a resource only under conditions of objective uncertainty stress. The specific nature of college or university education does not directly influence students' professional development and psychological well-being. However, the level of uncertainty stress and the expression of psychological resources are higher among university students than among college students. Conclusion: Thus, psychological resources for professional development and psychological well-being vary depending on the type of stress and enable Russian students to successfully overcome subjective and objective uncertainty stress.
